title: Landslide and Flash Flood Kill 6 in Kerala's Idukki Amid Heavy Rain Alerts
excerpt: Six people died in Idukki on Sunday as a landslide hit Kottakamboor in Vattavada and flash floods surged through the Chokkad River, while the IMD issued fresh rain alerts across Kerala.
body:
• At least six people died in Kerala's Idukki district on Sunday after a landslide struck Kottakamboor in Vattavada and a flash flood swept through the Chokkad River.
  • The bodies of a woman and two men were recovered after the landslide; the flash flood toll at Chokkad has risen to three, with several more people feared swept away.
  • About 27 people stranded mid-river were rescued by local residents and volunteers, while search teams continue looking for the missing.
  • The IMD has issued yellow alerts for seven districts and orange alerts for Idukki and Kottayam, warning of isolated heavy rainfall of up to 115.5 mm in 24 hours.

At least six people died in Kerala's Idukki district on Sunday after a landslide struck Kottakamboor in Vattavada and a flash flood surged through the Chokkad River, as the India Meteorological Department warned of more heavy rain across the state.

The bodies of a woman and two men who went missing in the landslide were recovered, while police said the death toll in the flash flood at Chokkad has risen to three. Search operations are continuing, with more people feared missing.

Context & Background

The landslide struck a temporary farm shed at Kottakamboor in Vattavada, where three people had taken shelter from intense afternoon rain. Two of them — Balakrishnan and his sister Chinnu — were killed, and Balakrishnan's wife Mariyamma was critically injured. A fallen electric pole landed on the structure, and investigators are examining whether electrocution played a role; post-mortem results are pending.

Local residents reached the hard-to-access site first, carrying the injured on makeshift bamboo stretchers, before Fire and Rescue teams from Munnar and Devikulam police arrived to take over the search. District authorities have ordered an inquiry and post-mortems, promised to cover medical bills and provide financial assistance to the victims' families.

The flash flood hit the Kottappuzha at TK Colony in Pookkottumpadam around 5 pm on Sunday. Preliminary reports say about seven people, including tourists and a local woman, were feared swept away; the body of a man aged around 50 was recovered from the river at Muttikkund in Pottikkallu and shifted to the District Hospital.

Because Sunday was a holiday, hundreds of tourists had gathered along the river — from Olarvattom Canal to T.K. Colony, Kettungal, Aanakkundu and Balawadippadi in the Koyipra foothills. As the water level rose suddenly, about 27 people stranded in the middle of the river were rescued by local residents and members of the Muhammad Suhail Treatment Aid Committee, while four people from Chokkad remained stranded on rocks and trees near an Anganwadi, unable to reach safety.

Impact & Analysis

The IMD has placed seven districts, including Thiruvananthapuram and Idukki, under a yellow alert for Sunday, with isolated heavy rainfall of up to 115.5 mm expected over 24 hours, and issued orange alerts for Idukki and Kottayam. In the high ranges, saturated slopes and sudden river surges leave little margin for error — a pattern Kerala has seen repeatedly during intense monsoon spells.

The disaster was not confined to Kerala: in Gangtok, Sikkim, continuous heavy rain triggered landslides, mudflows and road blockages, prompting the District Disaster Management Authority to begin a damage assessment across the district.

With searches still underway for those feared swept away, the death toll could rise. Police, Fire and Rescue Services, volunteers and residents are continuing joint operations.

Diaspora Angle

Kerala's large global diaspora follows monsoon news closely — for many families abroad, a disaster in Idukki means anxious hours trying to reach relatives in the high ranges. Sunday's events are a reminder to check on family back home, and for travelers to heed IMD alerts and stay away from riverbanks and hilly roads during heavy rain.

What's Next

Rescue teams will keep searching the Chokkad River for the missing as long as conditions allow. With orange and yellow alerts still in force, authorities are urging residents in landslide-prone and low-lying areas to stay alert, and saturated slopes mean the risk will persist until the rain eases.
